title: Tuchel recalls Ben White to the England squad for the first time since March
desc: Thomas Tuchel has brought Arsenal's Ben White back for England's Nations League games with Croatia and Spain after he missed the World Cup through injury.
body:
Thomas Tuchel has recalled Ben White to the England squad for November's UEFA Nations League fixtures, the Arsenal defender's first involvement since March, according to the FA's squad announcement.

The decision

White was ruled out of this summer's World Cup after an injury he sustained with Arsenal late last season, the FA said. Tuchel has now restored him to a 25 man group for the final two games of the Nations League group stage: Croatia at Wembley on Thursday 12 November and Spain in Madrid on Sunday 15 November, both kicking off at 7.45pm.

It is one of several returns in the squad. Djed Spence and Declan Rice are also back after missing the last camp through injury.

Why it matters for Tuchel

White gives the head coach an experienced defender who can play at right back or in the middle. The defensive group named alongside him includes Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarrad Branthwaite, Lewis Hall, Ezri Konsa, Jarell Quansah and Djed Spence, so the recall widens the options rather than handing White an automatic place.

Defensive cover has already been tested in this window. Marc Guehi has withdrawn through injury, with Dan Burn called up in his place, and Bournemouth's James Hill has since received a first senior call up, the FA's squad updates show. The FA has also said Konsa will not be in contention for the Croatia game. Those changes make an experienced, versatile defender more valuable to Tuchel this week.

What is at stake

England are second in Group C. Avoiding defeat against Croatia would be enough to secure a place in next March's quarter finals, while finishing top would require two wins and a better goal difference than Spain.

What to watch

The question now is whether Tuchel trusts White straight away against Croatia or eases him back in. With the World Cup behind them and the next tournament cycle starting, how often he picks White over the coming windows will show whether this is a short term call or a return to the core of the squad.

title: Tuchel hands first England call ups to Jobe Bellingham and Josh King
desc: Thomas Tuchel has promoted midfielders Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund and Fulham's Josh King from the under 21s for the Nations League games.
body:
Thomas Tuchel has given first senior England call ups to two young midfielders, Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund and Fulham's Josh King, for the final UEFA Nations League group games against Croatia and Spain, the FA's squad announcement confirmed.

The decision

Both players step up from the men's under 21 squad. King already has some experience around the senior group after travelling to the United States in the summer for England's pre World Cup training camp in Florida. Bellingham joins his under 21 teammate after impressing with his form at Dortmund in the Bundesliga in the early part of this season, the FA said.

The pair are among nine midfielders in Tuchel's 25 man squad, alongside Elliot Anderson, Jude Bellingham, James Garner, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Declan Rice, who returns after missing the last camp through injury.

Why Tuchel might make the move now

The timing gives Tuchel a low risk look at the next generation. These are the last two games of the group stage, England are second in Group C and a draw against Croatia at Wembley would be enough to secure a quarter final place next March. Bringing young players into camp at this stage lets the coaching staff assess them in training without building the squad around them.

It also means Jobe Bellingham joins his brother Jude in the senior squad for the first time.

The bigger picture

The squad still leans on experience. Captain Harry Kane could become England's most capped men's player if he features, having equalled Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps in the last window. Picking Bellingham and King alongside that core suggests Tuchel is planning for the next tournament cycle while keeping continuity.

What to watch

A call up is not a cap. The fixtures are Croatia at Wembley on Thursday 12 November and Spain in Madrid on Sunday 15 November, both at 7.45pm. Whether either midfielder gets minutes, and in which game, will show how quickly Tuchel intends to integrate them.

title: Arteta tells Premier League leaders Arsenal to be 'much more chaotic' against low blocks
desc: Arsenal are six points clear in the Premier League but have only 15 goals in ten games. After the 1-0 win over Hull, Mikel Arteta asked for less perfectionism and earlier goals.
body:
Mikel Arteta wants Arsenal to stop chasing the perfect goal. After the 1-0 Premier League win over Hull, the Arsenal manager said his side must be "much more chaotic" against deep defences, the Guardian reported.

"Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game."
Mikel Arteta, quoted by the Guardian, 9 November 2026

The decision in focus

This is a tactical instruction from Arteta rather than a change of personnel. He is asking his players to accept messier, more direct routes to goal when opponents sit deep, instead of working the ball until the ideal chance appears. He also wants them to score earlier, before matches settle into a pattern of Arsenal possession against a packed defence.

Why he is asking

The results are fine. Arsenal go into the international break six points clear of Manchester City at the top of the Premier League. The Guardian notes that the Hull game was their fourth one-goal league win of the season, and that they won 15 games by a single goal on the way to last season's title.

The goals are the concern. Arsenal have 15 in their first ten league matches. According to the Guardian, that puts them on course to beat the record for the fewest goals scored by a Premier League champion: 67, by Manchester United in 1992-93, the competition's first season. Arsenal have also struggled to score before half-time. Last month they went six matches in all competitions without a first-half goal, and Arteta has asked his players to be more ruthless.

How Decide Football reads it

Arteta has said publicly what the numbers already show. A side that leads the league by six points is still worried that its attack depends too much on control. The next Premier League matches after the break will show whether the message changes anything: more early goals, more shots from second balls and fewer games decided by one goal.

title: Le Bris's Sunderland overhaul pays off as Talbi starts and Black Cats beat Chelsea
desc: After Thursday's home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb, Régis Le Bris kept only Xhaka, Meunier and Roefs. Chemsdine Talbi made his first Premier League start of the season in a 1-0 win.
body:
Régis Le Bris made sweeping changes to his Sunderland side for Sunday's Premier League match against Chelsea, and they paid off with a 1-0 win that lifted the Black Cats off the bottom of the table.

The decision in focus

Sunderland had lost at home to Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday, a defeat the Guardian described as the "latest alarming performance" and one that "felt like a season watershed". Le Bris responded with what the Guardian called a "cull": only the captain, Granit Xhaka, Thomas Meunier and goalkeeper Robin Roefs kept their places.

Chemsdine Talbi was among those brought in, making his first Premier League start of the season. He had two "zesty incisions" in the opening quarter of an hour, according to the Guardian. The first led to a blocked shot from Trai Hume, and the second set up a clear chance for Brian Brobbey. Talbi also fired a shot just wide on the break late on.

How the match went

The rotation was tested within three minutes when Xhaka went off injured. Sunderland were also without Dan Ballard, who was injured, and Omar Alderete, who was suspended. The patched-up defence still kept Chelsea quiet. Enzo Le Fée scored the only goal from the penalty spot just after the half-hour, after Levi Colwill brought down Brobbey.

Le Bris pointed to Brobbey's role after the match. "Against a team that wants to press like that it's so important to have a target man," he said. He described the performance as "the identity, the intensity, the togetherness, the way we managed the game".

Why it matters

The Premier League's review notes that it was Sunderland's second league win of the season, with both coming at the Stadium of Light. It was also their third consecutive win over Chelsea. Their next four home league games are against Tottenham Hotspur, Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Hull City.

How Decide Football reads it

Le Bris used the Zagreb defeat as a reason to change almost the whole team rather than tinker with it, and the fresh side gave the Stadium of Light the intensity he wanted. The test now is whether he goes back to his first-choice players or keeps faith with the side that beat Chelsea.

title: Marco Rose's fast-start plan works as Bournemouth win eighth in a row at Ipswich
desc: Coming off a Europa League trip three days earlier, Marco Rose had Bournemouth ready to start quickly. They scored after five minutes at Ipswich and won 2-1 to equal a club record.
body:
Marco Rose made fast starts a priority for Bournemouth, and his side delivered at Portman Road. Evanilson scored after five minutes and Bournemouth beat Ipswich Town 2-1 in the Premier League on Sunday, their eighth consecutive win in all competitions, the Guardian reported.

The decision in focus

Bournemouth are playing European football for the first time this season, and the Ipswich match came three days after a Europa League win at Sparta Prague. The Guardian says Rose has been "working hard" to make sure his team are ready to start Premier League games quickly after a Thursday fixture.

Rose explained his reasoning by pointing to the cost of slow starts. "We played Chelsea four weeks ago and we were two down after three minutes," he said. "That's why we learned and always good to score an early goal." In the previous weekend's 2-0 home win against Leeds, Bournemouth had a goal ruled out after 11 minutes.

"Last week I said we start slow and this week I said we start quite quick and score an early goal. I am a magician!"
Marco Rose, quoted by the Guardian, 8 November 2026

How the game went

Evanilson's opener came after Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton tried and failed to dribble past him. Bournemouth went 2-0 up 27 seconds into the second half, when Leif Davis deflected Ryan Christie's shot into his own net. Jack Clarke pulled one back from the penalty spot with 17 minutes left after Lewis Cook tripped Abdoul Ouattara, but Bournemouth held on.

Rose said he was pleased with the first 70 minutes but "much more pleased with the last 20 minutes. We suffered but we did it together."

The numbers

Eight straight wins equals the club record set under Eddie Howe in 2012-13, a season that ended in promotion from League One. Evanilson has now scored in five consecutive Premier League matches. The Premier League says no Bournemouth player had done that before. With seven goals this season, he has already beaten his total for the whole of last season.

How Decide Football reads it

Rose identified slow starts as the risk of the Thursday-Sunday schedule and built his preparation around fixing them. At Ipswich it worked twice, with early goals in both halves. The test is whether Bournemouth can keep it up through a run of European and league fixtures.

title: Iraola leaves Gravenberch out of Liverpool's squad at Crystal Palace
desc: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool team sheet for the Premier League trip to Crystal Palace has no place for Ryan Gravenberch, two days after the head coach called the midfielder's heel problem a day-to-day pain decision.
body:
Andoni Iraola has left Ryan Gravenberch out of Liverpool's matchday squad for Sunday's Premier League game at Crystal Palace.

Liverpool posted the team on X on 8 November 2026. The starting XI listed in the club's graphic is Alisson, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez, Wirtz, Szoboszlai, Isak, Mac Allister, Gakpo, Barcola and Araujo. The substitutes are Mamardashvili, Gomez, Endo, Tsimikas, Munoz, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas and Ngumoha. Gravenberch is in neither list.

The decision in focus

On Friday Iraola had made Gravenberch's availability a question of pain tolerance. The club quoted him saying:

“Let's see if he can deal with the pain and if he can help us.”
Liverpool FC (@LFC), 6 November 2026

Liverpool's club write-up said the midfielder had a heel injury and was the only selection doubt. Sunday's team sheet answers that question: Gravenberch does not start and is not on the bench. Liverpool have not said, in the team post, whether he failed a late fitness test or was rested as a precaution.

How Decide Football reads it

Iraola had set out a simple rule on Friday: if Gravenberch could manage the pain, he would be involved. Leaving him out of the 20 entirely suggests the head coach decided the risk was not worth it for this Premier League fixture, with Mac Allister and Szoboszlai in the midfield he did pick. Any fuller explanation should come from Iraola's post-match comments.

title: Maresca says injury forced Guéhi and Gvardiol half-time changes in Premier League loss at Forest
desc: Enzo Maresca took off Marc Guéhi and Joško Gvardiol at half-time of Manchester City's 3-1 Premier League defeat at Nottingham Forest, saying both changes were injury related.
body:
Enzo Maresca replaced both Marc Guéhi and Joško Gvardiol at half-time of Manchester City's 3-1 Premier League defeat at Nottingham Forest on Saturday, and said afterwards that the double change was down to injury, NBC Sports reported.

“Marc Guehi asked for the change because of injury, Josko [Gvardiol] during the week had some small issues.”

The selection before kick-off

Maresca made three changes for the trip, with Rúben Dias, Gvardiol and Jérémy Doku coming into the starting XI and Matheus Nunes, Nico O'Reilly and Phil Foden dropping to the bench, according to City's team news. The back line in front of Gianluigi Donnarumma was Abdukodir Khusanov, Dias, Guéhi and Gvardiol. Losing two of those four at the interval meant reshaping the defence for the second half.

Injury, not a hook

Mistakes and slow play from both defenders had looked like the reason for the change, NBC Sports noted, but Maresca's explanation points to fitness rather than a tactical rebuke. He was also blunt about the first half as a whole, saying his side lost the duels and second balls and were 2-1 down by the time they tried to react.

What the decision leaves behind

The defeat was City's third straight in the Premier League and extended their run without a clean sheet to eight games, with former City prospect Liam Delap scoring twice for Forest. If Guéhi's problem lingers, NBC Sports pointed out, the defensive options behind him are thin, which makes the timing of the international break important for City. Maresca shrugged off the slump, pointing out that City had won their first seven games before losing three in a row.

title: Stephen Robinson's Aberdeen Future in Doubt After 4-0 Hibernian Defeat
desc: Stephen Robinson faces mounting pressure at Aberdeen after a 4-0 home defeat to Hibernian left the Dons in the Scottish Premiership relegation play-off place.
body:
Stephen Robinson's position as Aberdeen head coach is under intense scrutiny after a 4-0 defeat to Hibernian at Pittodrie on Saturday, 7 November 2026, left the Dons in the Scottish Premiership relegation play-off place.

Aberdeen supporters called for Robinson's dismissal during the second half, but the manager insisted after the match that he remained in charge and would continue fighting for results unless the club decided otherwise.

Robinson Responds to Calls for His Dismissal

Speaking to BBC Scotland following the defeat, Robinson acknowledged that the performance and result were unacceptable.

"I don't know [what the implications may be], I don't make that decision," he said.

"I'm Aberdeen manager until told otherwise, I'll keep fighting until told otherwise."

Robinson also expressed confidence in his managerial ability while acknowledging that decisions about his future rested with the club's leadership.

He said he had not received any indication immediately after the match that his position had changed and expected to speak with senior figures, as he regularly does.

According to the Press and Journal, Aberdeen supporters chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning" as Hibernian extended their lead.

The newspaper reported that Robinson and his players were booed at full-time, following another difficult home performance.

As of Sunday morning, no confirmed announcement of Robinson's dismissal or a formal board review had emerged from the sources checked. Any suggestion that a decision has already been taken would therefore be premature.

Four Goals Deepen Aberdeen's Problems

Hibernian arrived at Pittodrie bottom of the Scottish Premiership but left with an emphatic victory that lifted them above Aberdeen on goal difference.

Former Aberdeen midfielder Jamie McGrath opened the scoring with a long-range strike in the 57th minute.

Callum Wright doubled the visitors' advantage in the 79th minute after goalkeeper Marius Müller saved an effort from Thibault Klidjé.

Nicky Cadden added a third in the 87th minute before Klidjé completed the scoring in stoppage time.

Sky Sports reported that the defeat was Aberdeen's fifth in their previous six league matches.

The Dons had opportunities during the first half, including a Jack Milne header against the crossbar, but failed to capitalise before Hibernian took control.

Aberdeen's own match report acknowledged that the hosts wasted several first-half chances and were comfortably beaten by the visitors' more clinical second-half performance.

The result left Aberdeen 11th in the table after 12 league matches, level on 11 points with Hibernian but behind on goal difference.

What Happens Next for Robinson?

Robinson was appointed Aberdeen manager in March 2026 after establishing a strong reputation at St Mirren, where he achieved three successive top-six finishes and won the Scottish League Cup.

However, BBC Sport Scotland reported that he has won only six of his first 21 Scottish Premiership matches in charge of Aberdeen, losing 11.

The BBC also highlighted concerns about recruitment and tactical consistency following a summer in which Aberdeen brought in 15 players.

Former Aberdeen captain Willie Miller criticised the team's performance and recruitment during BBC Sportsound coverage, while former Scotland midfielder Michael Stewart suggested on Premier Sports that the scale of the defeat could prove decisive for Robinson's future.

Those assessments are opinions from pundits rather than indications of an official club decision.

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington, appointed in September, now faces questions about whether Robinson should remain in charge.

The international break offers the club an opportunity to assess its position without an immediate league fixture, although no formal timetable for a decision has been confirmed.

For Robinson, the immediate reality is clear: Aberdeen are in the relegation play-off position, supporters have openly demanded change, and the club's leadership must determine whether the current manager can reverse the decline.

title: Egypt sack Hossam Hassan and hand Ali Maher the national team job
desc: The Egyptian Football Association has dismissed head coach Hossam Hassan and appointed Ceramica Cleopatra manager Ali Maher before two Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Malawi.
body:
Egypt have sacked head coach Hossam Hassan and his staff and appointed Ali Maher to lead the national team, the Egyptian Football Association (EFA) announced on Saturday. It is a federation decision taken days before Egypt's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, part of the international calendar.

Arab News Sport reported the change on X:

"Egypt parts ways with coach Hossam Hassan, with Ali Maher named as his replacement, says @EFA"

What the federation said

In its statement, carried in English by CAF, the EFA board said it had reviewed "all the circumstances and events that have unfolded recently, along with their negative impact on the national team's positive image and stability" before deciding to part ways with Hassan and his technical and administrative staff.

The board thanked Hassan for his work and asked Maher to present his plan for a new coaching staff. The EFA did not set out in detail which events it meant.

Why the decision stands out

Hassan, Egypt's record goalscorer, had been in charge since February 2024. He led the Pharaohs to fourth place at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and to the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, CAF noted. Reuters, via CNA, reported that he had renewed his contract until 2030 after the World Cup and leaves after 38 matches: 21 wins, 10 draws and seven defeats.

Reuters also pointed to recent friction. Hassan's decision to substitute Mohamed Salah in the 60th minute of a 0-0 home draw with Angola in September came under scrutiny, and Hassan was given a three-match FIFA ban for criticising the referee after the World Cup defeat by Argentina.

What comes next

Maher, 52, leaves Ceramica Cleopatra to take over. Egypt play Malawi twice this month in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying, so the new head coach's first decisions on selection and staff will come almost immediately.

title: Arteta defends Declan Rice’s full 90 after Slavia Prague
desc: Mikel Arteta said Declan Rice’s full Champions League 90 minutes against Slavia Prague fitted the plan after a Fleetwood rest and a week’s recovery, rejecting overwork claims.
body:
Mikel Arteta has defended his decision to keep Declan Rice on for the full 90 minutes in Arsenal’s Champions League win away to Slavia Prague, saying the midfielder’s workload fitted the club’s recovery plan.

The decision

Asked after the 2-1 victory whether playing Rice for the entire match had been the plan, Arteta told Arsenal’s own transcript of the press conference: “The game required it, and he was also rested against Fleetwood. He had a week to recover before Liverpool, it’s his second game in a week and we expect our players to be able to do that.”

That answer is the managerial decision at the centre of this piece: Arteta chose minutes for Rice in Prague rather than protecting him with an earlier substitution, and he publicly justified the call with prior rest and recovery time.

League and competition context

The fixture sits in the UEFA Champions League, but Arteta’s comments also speak to Premier League selection pressure. The Guardian’s 6 November Premier League news roundup said Arteta insisted Rice is not being asked to play too many games and that Arsenal are managing his training load and minutes more carefully than in any previous season. Those are Arteta’s assurances as reported; they do not by themselves prove a lower minute total than last season.

Arsenal.com’s full presser transcript also covers Arteta’s criticism of a second-half drop-off, praise for Viktor Gyökeres and concern about the chances Slavia created. The Rice question is the selection call that matters for Decide Football’s manager-decision brief.

Why the call matters

Rice is central to how Arteta structures both Premier League and Champions League midfields. Playing him for 90 minutes on the road after a cup rest is a statement that the head coach trusts the recovery window more than the public fatigue narrative. The counter-risk is accumulation across a congested November. Arteta’s public answer puts the responsibility on planning: Fleetwood rest, a week before Liverpool, then a second start in seven days that he expects senior players to handle.

Until Arsenal’s next Premier League XI is named, the Prague full 90 remains the clearest recent evidence of how Arteta is balancing Rice’s Champions League and league demands.

title: Alonso delays Emi Martinez goalkeeper call until final session before Sunderland
desc: Xabi Alonso said Chelsea will decide after Saturday's final training whether Emi Martinez starts at Sunderland, with the goalkeeper back in sessions wearing protective headgear after jaw surgery.
body:
Xabi Alonso has pushed Chelsea's Premier League goalkeeper decision on Emi Martinez to the final pre-match session before Sunderland.

The club flagged the press conference on X on 6 November 2026:

Xabi Alonso with the latest on Emi Martinez and squad fitness ahead of Sunderland.
Chelsea FC (@ChelseaFC), 6 November 2026

Chelsea's official write-up quotes Alonso saying the Blues will decide after tomorrow's last training whether Martinez is fit, while noting he is training well in protective headgear after jaw surgery. Mike Penders has started the last three matches in his absence. Alonso also said Moises Caicedo will be checked after discomfort, and confirmed Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix and Joao Pedro are out.

The decision in focus

Alonso is choosing between a returning No.1 who has forced his way back ahead of schedule and a young keeper already on a three-game run. He called every positional call tough and said the final call comes after Saturday's session, then Sunday.

That is a concrete selection timeline for a Premier League away day at the Stadium of Light, not a vague fitness update.

How Decide Football reads it

Goalkeeper rotations after injury often leak early. Alonso instead set a public checkpoint: final training first, team sheet second. Until Chelsea publish the XI, the manager's stated rule is wait for Saturday's session before locking Martinez or Penders.

title: Iraola: Gravenberch a day-to-day pain call before Crystal Palace
desc: Andoni Iraola said Ryan Gravenberch is Liverpool's only selection doubt for the Premier League trip to Crystal Palace, framing the midfielder's heel issue as a matter of whether he can deal with the pain.
body:
Andoni Iraola has left Ryan Gravenberch's Premier League availability as a day-to-day pain decision ahead of Liverpool's trip to Crystal Palace.

The club posted his comments on X on 6 November 2026:

“Let's see if he can deal with the pain and if he can help us.”
Liverpool FC (@LFC), 6 November 2026

Liverpool's matching club write-up quotes Iraola saying Gravenberch is the only doubt and that the others will be the same as they have been. The midfielder missed the Champions League defeat by Fenerbahce with a heel injury and also sat out the preceding loss to Arsenal. Iraola called it a day-to-day matter of pain.

The decision in focus

This is a head coach's selection problem, not a vague fitness slogan. Iraola is publicly weighing whether Gravenberch can tolerate heel pain enough to help Liverpool at Selhurst Park. If the midfielder cannot, the XI changes; if he can, Iraola has signalled he wants him available.

That framing matters for Premier League minutes and for anyone projecting Liverpool's midfield three. Until the team sheet lands, the public logic is pain tolerance versus leaving him out.

How Decide Football reads it

Managers under injury doubt often hide behind “we'll see”. Iraola went further by naming Gravenberch as the lone question mark and by tying selection to pain management. Until results or the XI contradict him, that is the public decision rule for Sunday's Premier League fixture.

title: Maresca says City cannot use the same players across 60 to 65 games
desc: Enzo Maresca told Manchester City that rotation is unavoidable across a 60 to 65 game season, stressing that he is still learning his squad game by game.
body:
Enzo Maresca has publicly defended rotation at Manchester City, saying a season of 60 to 65 matches makes it impossible to field the same players every time.

The club posted his comments on X on 6 November 2026:

“The important thing is that, day after day, I know the players better. This is the best thing. It depends on the game, we have 60-65 games so it’s impossible to always use the same players. I’m quite lucky I have many good ones to choose from, depending on what we need for different games.”
Manchester City (@ManCity), 6 November 2026

The decision in focus

Maresca's point is a manager's selection problem, not a vague fitness slogan. He ties team picking to match demands and to a still growing feel for a large City squad. Knowing the players better day after day is, in his words, the best thing about the job right now.

That framing matters for Premier League weekends and midweek cups alike. When City rotate, Maresca wants the choice read as squad management across a heavy calendar, not as a vote of no confidence in whoever sits. He also stresses the luxury of options: many good players, chosen for what each game needs.

How Decide Football reads it

Managers under scrutiny for changed XIs often reach for fixture congestion. Maresca went further by putting a concrete 60 to 65 game band on the season and by owning the learning curve with his group. Until results turn against him, that is the public logic for why familiar names may sit and others start.

title: Arsenal push Arteta for Premier League Manager of the Month after a maximum points run
desc: Arsenal highlighted Mikel Arteta's nomination for the Premier League Manager of the Month award after a spell of maximum league points.
body:
Mikel Arteta is on the Premier League Manager of the Month shortlist, and Arsenal moved quickly to rally support behind their head coach.

The club posted on 5 November 2026:

“Maximum Premier League points 🤌 Mikel Arteta has been nominated for the @premierleague Manager of the Month award ❤️ You know what to do, Gooners 👇”
Arsenal (@Arsenal), 5 November 2026

Why the nomination fits the decision story

Manager of the Month is an award vote, but for Decide Football it is also a public verdict on recent selection and game plans. Arsenal's own framing ties the nod to a run of maximum Premier League points, the cleanest on pitch case a club can put behind its coach.

Arteta's recent league work includes the one nil win at Anfield that took Arsenal top, a result built on an early Kai Havertz goal and a shut down that left Liverpool without a shot on target. Nominations do not lock trophies, yet they freeze a moment when the league's own monthly award machinery is recognising that spell.

What happens next

The Premier League will publish the winner through its usual channels. Until then, Arsenal's post is campaigning, not crowning. The decision angle stays on Arteta: keep the same standards in selection and structure that produced the maximum points run the club is advertising.

title: Scott Parker's half-time triple change sparks West Ham comeback at Cardiff
desc: West Ham recovered from 3-0 down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff after Scott Parker made a triple substitution at half time in his first match in charge.
body:
Scott Parker's first match as West Ham head coach produced an immediate test of his authority and tactical judgement, as a half time triple substitution helped turn a 3-0 deficit at Cardiff into a 3-3 draw.

Cardiff's Jack Moylan scored a first half hat trick, leaving West Ham facing defeat in Parker's opening game in charge. The Guardian reported that Parker responded by making three changes at the interval, and West Ham produced a markedly improved second half.

The half-time triple change

The comeback was completed when Max Kilman scored eight minutes from time, according to the Guardian's match report. The draw rescued a point after a difficult opening 45 minutes and gave Parker an early example of the character he wants from his team.

Parker had only just taken the job after West Ham dismissed Nuno Espírito Santo. The club confirmed his appointment on a two and a half year contract on Wednesday, and the Cardiff fixture became his first opportunity to work with the squad in a competitive match.

What it means for Parker

The result was not an uncomplicated success. West Ham had conceded three times before the break, exposing defensive problems that a single comeback could not erase. The Guardian's subsequent report on Parker's return noted that the team still needed more complete performances if it was to challenge for automatic promotion from the Championship.

The half time changes nevertheless gave the new manager an immediate point of reference. West Ham showed that they could respond to adversity, but the scale of the first half collapse also underlined the work required to become a consistent promotion contender.

For Parker, the match was an unusually compressed introduction to the demands of the job. His appointment was built partly on a record of taking Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley out of the Championship. The Cardiff comeback supplied a dramatic opening, but the season will be judged on whether he can turn that response into repeatable performances.

title: Aston Villa and Unai Emery commit beyond 2029 as new deal talks continue
desc: Aston Villa say chairman Nassef Sawiris and Unai Emery have reached a clear commitment beyond 2029. Fabrizio Romano reports a new contract is moving to the final stages, while BBC Sport says fine details are still being settled and an announcement is unlikely before the weekend.
body:
Aston Villa have publicly tied Unai Emery into the next phase of the club's project after a working meeting between the head coach and the hierarchy. The Premier League club said chairman Nassef Sawiris met Emery with president of football operations Roberto Olabe and director of football operations Damian Vidagany to plan the club's long-term sporting direction.

“Aston Villa offered new contract to Unai Emery, same for Damian Vidagany and Roberto Olabe: deal moving to final stages.”
— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano), 5 November 2026

What the club said

Villa's statement said the talks established "a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery" and framed the aim as building an ambitious, competitive side. The club did not publish a signed contract length, salary figures or a completion date in that statement.

Where the talks stand

BBC Sport reported that Emery is close to agreeing a contract extension that would hand him even more responsibility for long-term development, with talks still ongoing about the fine details, the finances and the length of the new deal. BBC Sport said the plan is to announce the new contract once those details are agreed, and that an announcement is unlikely before the weekend. Emery was already under contract until 2029, according to that report.

Romano's update said Villa want to close the door on interest from other clubs and are very happy with Emery, with matching contract progress for Vidagany and Olabe. That reporting describes talks advancing, not a completed signature.

Context around Manchester United interest

BBC Sport noted Emery has been linked with Manchester United, who Villa play this weekend at Old Trafford, should United sack Michael Carrick. The same piece said Villa previously threatened pundit Jamie Carragher with legal action after he suggested Emery would be a good United option, then dropped the threat after an apology. Those links help explain why Villa are stressing continuity now; they do not, on their own, confirm a signed extension.

What is settled, and what is not

What is on the record today is a club commitment beyond 2029 and reporting that a longer deal is close. What is not confirmed in the cited sources is that Emery has signed the new contract, or the exact years and wages. Until Villa announce those terms, the story is a public commitment and advanced talks rather than a finished deal.

title: Bruno Fernandes Backs Carrick’s Call to Drop Him After Roma Comeback
desc: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says Michael Carrick was right to bench him after his tactics criticism, following the 3-2 Champions League win over Roma.
body:
Michael Carrick's decision to drop his captain has been endorsed by the player himself. After Manchester United came from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the UEFA Champions League league phase at Old Trafford on Tuesday night, Bruno Fernandes said his manager was right to put him on the bench last month, even if it was a punishment for his public criticism of United's tactics. BBC Sport reported it was the first time Fernandes had spoken to the media since being dropped.

“Bruno: Right to bench me after criticism of Man United tactics”
— ESPN FC (@ESPNsoccer), 3 November 2026

The decision

After United's previous Champions League match, a 4-1 defeat at Como, Fernandes blamed Carrick for the side's lack of pressing in a post-match interview, according to The Independent. Carrick responded by leaving him as an unused substitute for the next match, a 3-0 Premier League defeat at Bournemouth. Fernandes was restored to the side for the Premier League defeat by Chelsea, and against Roma he converted a twice-taken 58th-minute penalty that started the comeback before two goals from Matheus Cunha completed it, as The Guardian reported.

Why Fernandes says it was right

Speaking to Amazon Prime after the match, Fernandes said: “It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air, then after that the manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I'm not performing. That's fair.”

He added: “Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. And, if it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. It doesn't change the belief I have of the manager and the staff and every player in this club.”

That matters for Carrick. A manager who drops his captain for speaking out risks losing the dressing room; instead, the captain has publicly backed the authority behind the call and responded with his best display of the season, according to ESPN.

Still under pressure

The win ended a run of nine matches without a victory, but it does not settle Carrick's position. United sit 17th in the Premier League with one win from their opening nine games, and BBC Sport reported that Carrick had been widely expected to be sacked after the Bournemouth defeat before the board decided he deserved a chance to turn things around. Carrick was given a two-year contract after winning 12 of his 17 games in charge last season.

Fernandes rejected the idea that the result was about one man. “We don't need to save anyone's job,” he said. “The club needed that win, the players needed that win.” Youri Tielemans was more direct when asked the same question: “That's a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.”

For now, the selection call that looked like a gamble a fortnight ago has the captain's public approval and a Champions League win attached to it. Whether it buys Carrick time depends on what follows in the Premier League.

title: How Arteta's game plan stopped Liverpool from landing a shot on target at Anfield
desc: Arsenal scored early through Kai Havertz, then shut Liverpool out – 17 attempts, none on target – to win at Anfield for the first time since 2012.
body:
Mikel Arteta's Arsenal won 1-0 at Liverpool on Sunday 1 November, their first win at Anfield since 2012 and the end of a run of 16 visits without a victory there.

The goal came in the 16th minute. Martin Odegaard cut out a clearance from Alisson, the ball was moved on to Declan Rice on the right, and his low cross was tapped in at the far post by Kai Havertz.

After that, Arsenal's approach was about protecting the lead. Liverpool had 17 attempts but none forced David Raya into a save. According to Arsenal, it was the first time on record that Liverpool failed to land a shot on target in a Premier League game at Anfield. Jurrien Timber made important blocks. Sky Sports noted that officials missed a tug by Timber on Alexander Isak in the first half which might have led to a penalty.

The result took Arsenal top of the Premier League with 24 points from nine games, three points clear of Manchester City and nine clear of Liverpool. Havertz's goal also made him the top-scoring German in Premier League history, with 46. Arsenal's next game is away to Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday.

title: Carrick under pressure: the Martinez question and a nine-game winless run
desc: Manchester United are winless in nine and 17th in the Premier League. Michael Carrick insists the dressing room is in a good place.
body:
Michael Carrick goes into Manchester United's Champions League game with Roma under heavy pressure. Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, in which Lisandro Martinez was sent off, extended United's winless run to nine games in all competitions. Radio Times reports United have not had such a run since 1988.

United are 17th in the Premier League, above the relegation zone only on goal difference, and have lost their last two Champions League games, to Atletico Madrid and Como, the second of them 4-1.

Radio Times reported that Carrick was given the club's backing last week, but that another defeat at Old Trafford could cost him his job. At Monday's press conference, Carrick said: “The dressing room is in a good place.”

One decision in focus is whether to keep picking Martinez. His red card ban covers domestic games only, but Sports Illustrated argued that his form this season means he “has to come out of the team”.

Roma, managed by Gian Piero Gasperini, arrive unbeaten in Serie A this season with seven wins and three draws.

title: Danks Faces Neuer and Olise Calls for Bayern’s Atlético Champions League Trip
desc: Interim Bayern Munich coach Aaron Danks must decide whether returning players Manuel Neuer and Michael Olise are ready to start against Atlético Madrid.
body:
Aaron Danks faces two distinct selection questions before Bayern Munich's UEFA Champions League trip to Atlético Madrid: who should start in goal and whether Michael Olise is ready for a starting role. Bavarian Football Works reports that both Olise and Manuel Neuer returned to training, but their availability for the match will depend on fitness assessments and workload. Jonas Urbig also trained, leaving the goalkeeper decision open ahead of matchday.

The uncertainty is significant because Bayern are operating without manager Vincent Kompany on the touchline. The National reports that Kompany is recovering after a collapse at the club's training ground and a diagnosis of meningeal irritation. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the absence would be measured in weeks rather than days. Danks therefore has responsibility for the immediate match decisions during an unusually sensitive period for the club.

Danks also needs to fill an attacking-midfield role with Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry unavailable, according to Bavarian Football Works. He indicated that the player chosen should make use of his own qualities rather than attempt to imitate an absent team-mate. That is a meaningful tactical distinction: replacing a name on the team sheet does not necessarily mean asking the replacement to perform the same movements or occupy every space in the same way.

The goalkeeper question is more straightforward in its options but still difficult in practice. Neuer's return to training makes him a possibility, while Urbig has also been involved. The report says Bayern planned to decide after assessing both keepers on matchday. Training participation alone is not confirmation that Neuer will start, and Danks has not been reported as announcing a final choice in the cited preview. Any article claiming a confirmed goalkeeper from those comments would overstate the evidence.

The Champions League context raises the stakes. Bayern had drawn their previous two European matches, according to The National, and Danks said finishing in the top eight of the league phase was a target because it offers direct passage to the round of 16. That ambition does not determine his selection automatically: a returning player might strengthen the side but also carry workload considerations. The decision requires balancing immediate competitiveness with readiness.

Bayern's recent results show that the side has continued to function without Kompany in the dugout. The National lists a 3-1 Bundesliga win at Freiburg, a 6-1 German Cup victory against Magdeburg and a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund. Those results provide context for Danks' responsibility but do not answer whether the same selections are appropriate against Atlético. Opponent, venue and available personnel all change the calculation.

Danks has signalled that Bayern will retain an aggressive approach, seeking to play on the front foot and regain possession quickly. Bavarian Football Works also reports his recognition of Atlético's possession improvements, defensive strength and cohesion. That makes the choice of attacking midfielder especially important: Bayern need a player who can contribute to their own forward play without undermining their ability to counter-press when possession changes.

The central story is not a speculative predicted XI. It is that Danks must make a set of connected decisions about Neuer, Urbig, Olise and an attacking-midfield vacancy while Kompany remains absent. Those choices will become verifiable when the official line-up is published; until then, the manager's stated criteria and the available squad information are the sound basis for analysis.

title: West Ham Appoint Scott Parker as Head Coach After Sacking Nuno
desc: West Ham have named Scott Parker head coach on a two-and-a-half-year deal, with his first Championship match away at Cardiff City on Wednesday.
body:
West Ham United have appointed Scott Parker as head coach, a day after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo. The former Hammers captain, 46, has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract and will take charge for Wednesday evening's EFL Championship match away at Cardiff City, the club confirmed.

“West Ham United can confirm that Scott Parker has agreed a deal to become the Club’s new men’s first-team Head Coach 🤝”
— West Ham United (@WestHam), 4 November 2026

Why Parker

West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season, and the board's aim is an immediate return. Parker's record fits the brief: he won promotion from the Championship to the Premier League with Fulham in 2020, Bournemouth in 2022 and Burnley in 2025, and was named EFL Championship Manager of the Season in 2024/25 with Burnley. Interim chief executive Karim Virani said he was "the unanimous choice of the Board".

"I've been in this division three times and I've got out of this division three times," Parker told the club's website. "This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it." He said consistency would be "the key word for all of us".

Where West Ham stand

Nuno left on Tuesday after back-to-back home defeats, 3-2 to Southampton and 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion, leaving the pre-season promotion favourites eighth in the Championship, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough, BBC Sport reported. The club said a "thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season" had led to the change, according to The Independent.

A familiar face

Parker made 129 appearances for West Ham between 2007 and 2011 and was named Hammer of the Year three times in a row. First-team coaches Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine will assist him, while his former team-mate Mark Noble will work closely with him. The club said further details of his permanent backroom staff would follow.

His first test comes straight away at Cardiff, with little time on the training ground. The bigger job is turning a stuttering campaign back into a promotion push.

title: Carrick's Shea Lacey Substitution Turns Manchester United's Champions League Comeback Against Roma
desc: Michael Carrick brought on 19-year-old Shea Lacey at 2-1 down against Roma, and the academy graduate set up Matheus Cunha's winner in a 3-2 Champions League victory.
body:
Michael Carrick's decision to bring on 19-year-old Shea Lacey for Amad in the 75th minute helped turn Manchester United's Champions League match against Roma. With United 2-1 down at Old Trafford on Tuesday night, the academy graduate came on and, according to the BBC, set up Matheus Cunha's 86th-minute winner in a 3-2 victory that ended a nine-game winless run.

“Shea Lacey, the 19-year-old academy graduate, could be in line for first Premier League start on Sunday after game-changing cameo in Champions League win over Roma”
— Times Sport (@TimesSport), 4 November 2026

The situation when Carrick made the change

Roma had been 2-0 up inside 17 minutes. Matías Soulé scored in the 11th minute and Donyell Malen converted a penalty six minutes later. Bruno Fernandes pulled one back from the penalty spot in the 58th minute, but United were still a goal behind when Carrick sent Lacey on for Amad with a quarter of an hour left, Sky Sports reported.

Cunha equalised in the 83rd minute and scored again three minutes later. The BBC credits Lacey with the assist for the second. Cunha was then sent off for a second yellow card in the first minute of stoppage time, and United held on with ten men.

What Carrick said

Carrick praised the teenager after the match, in comments reported by the BBC:

“Delighted for Shea. Love him to bits, he's so talented, he's desperate to do well. It's such a good pick out, Matheus takes it on his back foot. We moved Matheus inside second half and put Bryan wide left to give us better balance... he was even defending at right-back at the end!”

So the Lacey change came alongside a wider second-half reshuffle. Carrick moved Cunha inside in the second half and put Bryan wide left, which he said gave the side better balance. Lacey's arrival then added a fresh attacking option for the final 15 minutes.

Carrick has also faced questions this week over leaving Fernandes on the bench at the start, a call the captain has since publicly backed after the Roma comeback. Taken together, the two decisions show a manager willing to make big selection calls in a game United could not afford to lose.

Will Lacey start on Sunday?

According to Times Sport, Lacey could be in line for his first Premier League start on Sunday. That is a report, not a confirmed team selection, and Carrick has not named his side.

The case for him is simple: he came on with United losing and helped create the winning goal. The question for Carrick is whether one impact cameo is enough to hand a 19-year-old a league start, or whether Lacey's best use for now is the role he played against Roma, coming off the bench to change a game late on. The team sheet on Sunday will give the answer.

title: Allegri Rules Out Punitive Ritiro After Porto Thrash Napoli 4-1 in the Champions League
desc: Massimiliano Allegri said Napoli will not go into a ritiro after a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Porto, blaming set pieces and fatigue ahead of Serie A leaders Lazio.
body:
Massimiliano Allegri has ruled out, for now, taking Napoli into a punitive ritiro, a closed training retreat, after their 4-1 Champions League defeat by Porto at the Estádio do Dragão on Wednesday night. Instead he defended his players and pointed to set pieces and tiredness. It was Napoli's seventh defeat in 14 games this season, Corriere dello Sport reported.

The table after four games

Francesco Farioli's Porto left Napoli 27th in the Champions League league phase, with three points from four matches. It was their third defeat in four European games, Il Mattino noted. Their remaining fixtures are away at Manchester City, then Club Brugge, Sabah and Viking. Porto's first and third goals both came from corners, ANSA reported.

What Allegri said

Speaking to Prime Video after the match, Allegri said (translated from Italian):

“There have been games where I could have got angry, but today we played a good game for 70 minutes. … I'm certainly disappointed, bitter, because it's a bad moment. But tonight I have nothing to reproach the players for, for the dedication and the desire they showed.”
— Massimiliano Allegri, via ANSA (translated)

He said the set pieces had to be looked at: “We need to analyse the dead-ball situations, because that's where we conceded. These are details that make the difference” (translated, via ANSA).

He also blamed fatigue and a short squad. “You play every three days, at 70 minutes I couldn't make changes,” he said, adding that there was “a bit of tiredness from playing 70 minutes on an open pitch” (translated, via Corriere dello Sport).

Why no ritiro

Asked about strong decisions, Allegri said (translated, via Corriere dello Sport):

“No, not the ritiro… We've been away for six days, tomorrow we have to go home. Then on Friday we'll train and on Sunday there's a very important game for the league.”

Il Mattino's version of the same answer ends with the team training on Friday “and we'll decide”, and ANSA describes the ritiro as ruled out “for the moment”. So the door is not fully shut if results keep going the wrong way.

Under Pressure: Lazio next

Sunday's Serie A game is a big one. Napoli host league leaders Lazio, coached by Gennaro Gattuso, at the Maradona on Sunday morning. After that comes the international break, and Allegri said he expects to get some injured players back after it.

On social media, some Napoli fans called for Allegri to go after the defeat. But there have been no reports that the club is considering a change. Allegri has chosen trust over punishment. If Napoli lose to Lazio as well, he will be under more pressure going into the break.

title: Klopp Recalls Füllkrug and Hands Mohya, 17, a First Germany Call-Up for the Nations League
desc: Jürgen Klopp has named a 24-man Germany squad for the Nations League games against Serbia and the Netherlands, recalling Bundesliga top scorer Niclas Füllkrug and calling up 17-year-old Wael Mohya.
body:
Jürgen Klopp has made his biggest selection calls yet as Germany head coach, recalling Niclas Füllkrug and handing a first senior call-up to 17-year-old Borussia Mönchengladbach midfielder Wael Mohya in a 24-man squad for November's UEFA Nations League matches, the DFB announced on Thursday.

The fixtures

Germany play Serbia in Belgrade on 13 November and the Netherlands at the Olympiastadion in Berlin on 16 November in Nations League Group A2.

Form over reputation

Füllkrug returns after more than a year away from the national side. He leads the Bundesliga scoring chart with nine goals and has 14 goals in 24 international appearances, Bundesliga.com reported. Nick Woltemade, now on loan at Juventus from Newcastle United, is not included.

A teenager in the squad

Mohya, who has two caps for Germany's under-21s, is one of three uncapped players in the squad, alongside Brajan Gruda and Finn Jeltsch. Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry are unavailable through injury.

The decision tells us that Klopp is prepared to pick on current Bundesliga form rather than past selection, and to promote young players straight from the under-21 level.

title: Iraola Defends Five Changes After Liverpool Lose 3-2 at Fenerbahçe in the Champions League
desc: Andoni Iraola benched Wirtz, Isak and Gakpo for Liverpool's Champions League trip to Fenerbahçe and insisted rotation was not why they lost 3-2, blaming three set-piece goals.
body:
Andoni Iraola has defended his decision to make five changes to his Liverpool side for Wednesday's Champions League match at Fenerbahçe, which ended in a 3-2 defeat and the loss of their 100 per cent record in the competition.

The decision

Coming off a 1-0 Premier League defeat by Arsenal, Iraola started Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo on the bench, bringing in Dominik Szoboszlai, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz, beIN Sports reported. Bradley Barcola led the line.

"We put in Victor and Rio, they were more fresh. We thought also that for Alex it was maybe good to play 30 minutes, not more," Iraola said, according to Liverpool's official website. He admitted Barcola "has been better when he has played outside wide".

What happened

Trey Nyoni, with his first goal for the club, and the substitute Isak twice put Liverpool ahead. Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown equalised each time, and Vedat Muriqi scored the winner in the 79th minute, This Is Anfield reported.

His defence

"We've been doing it all season and all the games we've played midweek. I think we've been changing at least four, five, six, seven players. Because of the schedule that we have, it's impossible to maintain with always the [same] starting XI," Iraola said. "I trust the squad to sustain the level. I don't think it was the main reason why we lost."

He pointed instead to set pieces: "The main reason I can find to lose the game is we conceded [from] three set-pieces." Fenerbahçe scored from a free-kick, a corner and a long throw.

title: Reedijk's Wide-Left Call on Boyle Pays Off as Hibs Beat Hearts at Hampden
desc: Hibs head coach Marink Reedijk, who had taken the captaincy from Martin Boyle, played him in an unfamiliar wide-left role in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and Boyle scored in a 2-1 win over Hearts.
body:
Marink Reedijk caught Hearts off guard by playing Martin Boyle in an unfamiliar wide-left role in Sunday's Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and the Scottish Premiership side's forward responded with the goal that helped Hibs to a 2-1 win and a place in the final, the Edinburgh Evening News reported. It was Boyle's sixth goal in Edinburgh derbies.

Two calls on Boyle

The new head coach had already made a bold leadership decision, naming German right-back Felix Passlack captain ahead of Boyle, who had worn the armband consistently for two years while club captain Joe Newell was injured. Hibs had lost three and drawn one of Reedijk's opening matches before Hampden.

Boyle, who had missed the previous two games against Celtic and St Mirren with illness, said he was told on Saturday morning that he would start. "I didn't expect that," he said of the position. "It was kind of a free role, you can stay high and wide out there and can hit them where it hurts."

No grudge over the armband

Boyle said Reedijk had explained the captaincy change to him. "It didn't affect me one single bit," he said. "If that is the way forward he wants to go, then we will need to back the manager." Of the derby, he added: "Fair play to him on Sunday, he got it spot on."
